summary: iter399: tested the organisation-scoped Backup & Restore (System Console > Data & Backup) and the owner-level organisation export/import, through the API (pytest, 18 tests) and the UI (Playwright). The core isolation works. Previews and archives hold only the signed-in organisation's rows. Replace mode deletes only rows with that organisation's id, and 58:12 Global's per-collection counts were identical before and after a Lubwamas merge import and a Lubwamas replace import. A wrong password returns 401 and writes nothing. A dry run writes nothing and creates no snapshot. Each organisation sees only its own snapshots; another organisation gets 404 when downloading them, and so do old snapshots without an organisation id. A row id belonging to another organisation is rejected with a duplicate-key error (E11000) and the other row is left alone. Speed: a 58:12 export with files is 226MB and takes 24.6s through the API and 35s in the browser, with no 502 (79 files included, 233 over the cap). The owner-level export streams: 0.2s for Lubwamas records only, 0.7s for 58:12 records only, and 17.6-30s for 58:12 with files (248MB of valid JSON). The owner-level import of a Lubwamas export with files created a new organisation (lubwamas-1) with a fresh id, restoring 151/151 rows and 26/26 files with no failures and no change to Lubwamas. I deleted that organisation afterwards. Four real defects were found: (1) an archive can write files to ANY storage path, including another organisation's; (2) the scheduler's daily auto-backup is broken because it imports _build_tarball, which no longer exists; (3) restored files are saved as application/octet-stream; (4) the preview counts are misleading with the default options.

critical.issue: SECURITY / cross-organisation write: file restore writes every uploads/<path> entry in the archive back to storage at that exact path. The only check is that the path does not contain '..'. There is no check that the path belongs to the caller's organisation or that any imported row refers to it. An organisation admin can therefore build an archive that overwrites another organisation's logo, ID scans or receipts (e.g. uploads/branding/<other-org-id>/logo.png). Proven with a harmless path: a Lubwamas archive holding uploads/TEST_iter399_probe/not-referenced.txt (a path no organisation owns) returned uploads_restored=1. Fix: restore only paths that appear in the archive's own rows after organisation stamping, and/or require the path to be under an organisation-owned prefix, and/or refuse to overwrite an existing object owned by another organisation.

The daily 00:00 auto-backup is broken. scheduler.py:204 runs `from routers.backup import _build_tarball`, but the rewrite removed _build_tarball (now _stream_tarball(org_id, ...)). The ImportError is caught and logged as 'backup module unavailable', so no daily backup is written. The function would also need to run once per organisation and include the organisation id in the filename. The existing auto-daily-*.tar.gz files in /app/backend/backups are old whole-database dumps that hold every organisation's data; they cannot be downloaded through the API (filtered by organisation id) but should be pruned or protected.

minor.issue: Restored files are saved with put_object(rel, blob, 'application/octet-stream'). Lubwamas branding PNGs restored earlier are now served by /api/storage as application/octet-stream with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so opening them in a tab downloads them and PDFs will not preview. Guess the type with mimetypes.guess_type(rel), or store the content type in the manifest.

The preview counts audit collections and the files they link to even though 'Include audit' is unticked by default. Lubwamas preview shows 7 collections / 151 docs / 26 linked files, but the default export holds 6 collections / 19 docs / 0 files, because all 26 file links are inside audit_log rows. For 58:12 the preview shows 14,588 docs while the default export has 6,913. Show counts for the selected options, or split out the audit numbers.

The whole upload is read into memory (1GB cap). The rollback snapshot and the file writes happen inside the same request, so importing a 226MB archive with files is likely to exceed the 60s gateway limit. Not tested on 58:12 to avoid rewriting its data.
Takes a whole JSON dict in the body. A 58:12 export with files is 248MB, so re-importing it will probably hit body-size or time limits. Not tested, to avoid creating a large copy.

By design, notifications (16,978 rows for 58:12), push_subscriptions, security_pair_attempts and fingerprint_data are left out of the Backup & Restore archive but included in the owner export (31,653 vs 14,588 docs). Leaving out fingerprint_data means biometric enrolments are lost after a move. Confirm this is intended.

issues: The toast says '249 file(s) could not be read and are listed in the export', but most of those were left out by the 150MB cap, not because they were unreadable. The wording is misleading. There is also no records-only option for the owner-level export in the UI.
The snapshot Download buttons have no data-testid (only the row has backup-snapshot-<filename>).
When the dialog opens, the preview counts do not match what the default export contains (see the backend minor issue).

action_items: HIGH: in import_backup, restrict which file paths can be restored: only paths referenced by the imported organisation-stamped rows, or under an organisation-owned prefix, and never overwrite another organisation's object.

HIGH: fix scheduler._fire_auto_backup. Replace _build_tarball with a loop over organisations that writes _stream_tarball(org_id, True, system_user, include_files=False) to auto-daily-<org_id>-<stamp>.tar.gz, and remove or protect the old whole-database auto-daily archives.
Restore files with a guessed content type instead of application/octet-stream.
Make the preview follow the include_audit/include_files options, or show the audit counts separately.
Change the owner-export toast to tell 'over the size cap' apart from 'unreadable', and optionally add a records-only toggle.
critical_code_review_comments: backup.py import: in replace mode, delete_many({organization_id}) runs per collection BEFORE that collection's rows are parsed, so a corrupt JSONL file leaves the collection empty. The snapshot helps, but checking the rows first would be safer.
backup.py import: replace mode on 'users' deletes and re-inserts the importing admin's own row; if the archive does not include that admin, they lock themselves out.

Row ids are unique across the whole database (E11000 seen), so a Backup & Restore archive cannot be restored into a different organisation on the same server: every row whose id still exists elsewhere fails. This is acceptable for 'move between deployments', but the UI should say so.

organizations.py defines FILE_URL_RE and MAX_EXPORT_FILE_BYTES after the functions that use them (fine at runtime, poor readability). backup.py and organizations.py both have near-duplicate file-walking and file-batching code (DRY).

success_rate.backend: 94% (17/18; the 1 failure is the real cross-organisation file-path write)

seed_data_creation: No permanent seed data. Created then deleted: the organisation lubwamas-1 and all its rows (deleted by its own new id). Temporary members rows matching a 58:12 member id were deleted using organisation_id=Lubwamas (none were inserted, E11000). Left behind: a harmless 5-byte object TEST_iter399_probe/not-referenced.txt in object storage (storage has no delete function); new Lubwamas prerestore-* snapshots in /app/backend/backups; audit_log entries.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run /app/backend/tests/test_iter399_org_backup_export_import.py (about 70s with the two large with-files tests; deselect them with -k 'not with_files_no_502 and not global_with_files_export' for a quick run). It reads Mongo directly to compare per-collection counts per organisation. After the file-path fix, test_archive_can_write_arbitrary_file_path should pass (uploads_restored == 0). Lubwamas: 6 collections / 19 docs without audit; all 26 linked files are only in audit_log. UI: login, open /admin, click sysconsole-tab-data, then backup-restore-card. Owner UI: /organizations, export-org-<slug>.
